subject: history
title: Civil War, NEP and Stalin's Rise
welcome_lead: From Brest-Litovsk to Stalin's defeat of the Right Opposition.
meta_desc: -Level adventure on the Russian Civil War 1918-21, NEP and Stalin's rise to power 1924-29.
final_note: You can explain how Stalin emerged victorious in the succession struggle.

concepts.def: Peace signed 3 March 1918 with Germany; ceded Poland, Ukraine, Baltic states and Finland.
1918-21 emergency policy: forced grain requisitioning, nationalisation, labour conscription.
March 1921 sailors' rising demanding 'Soviets without Bolsheviks', forcing the move to NEP.
Tax in kind replaced requisitioning; small-scale private trade legalised.
December 1922 dictation criticising leading Bolsheviks; postscript called for Stalin's removal as General Secretary.
Stalin and Bukharin's doctrine (1924-25) of building socialism in the USSR alone, rejecting Trotsky's permanent revolution.

walkthroughs.body_html: Brest-Litovsk bought peace at great cost. Trotsky built the Red Army (over 5 million by 1920). Whites under Kolchak, Denikin, Yudenich and Wrangel were defeated piecemeal. Allied intervention failed. The Romanovs were murdered at Ekaterinburg (16-17 July 1918). The Cheka enforced Red Terror.

By 1921 industrial output stood at ~20% of 1913. The Kronstadt Mutiny and Tambov rising prompted NEP. The Tenth Party Congress (March 1921) banned factions. The 1921-22 famine killed perhaps 5 million; American Relief Administration aid was accepted. The USSR was constituted in December 1922. Lenin died on 21 January 1924; Petrograd became Leningrad.

Stalin used the General Secretaryship (from April 1922) to control appointments. The Triumvirate of Stalin-Zinoviev-Kamenev defeated Trotsky (Left Opposition, expelled 1927). Stalin then turned on the Right (Bukharin, Rykov, Tomsky) over the 1927 grain crisis, defeating them by 1929. By his 50th birthday (21 December 1929), Stalin was unchallenged.

mcqs.q: Which 1921 mutiny prompted the introduction of NEP?
options: Kronstadt Mutiny
Potemkin Mutiny
Tambov Rising
July Days

mcqs.q: What did Lenin's Testament urge regarding Stalin?
options: His removal as General Secretary
His promotion to Premier
His exile to Siberia
His marriage to Krupskaya
Stalin took power by leading the Red Army to victory in the Civil War.
Stalin took power because Lenin nominated him as his successor.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
No — Lenin's Testament (1922-23) warned against Stalin's rudeness and recommended his removal; Stalin won by manoeuvring against Trotsky after Lenin's death.

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: Stalin took power by leading the Red Army to victory in the Civil War.
War Communism had collapsed the economy and provoked the Kronstadt revolt; the NEP allowed limited private trade to restore production and stabilise Bolshevik rule.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
The NEP was Lenin's plan to permanently switch Russia to capitalism.

mcqs.q: What caused the English Civil War?
options: It was caused by Henry VIII's break with Rome.
It was caused by Charles I trying to arrest five MPs in 1642.
Stalin took power by leading the Red Army to victory in the Civil War.
Long-term tensions over royal absolutism, religion (Laudian reforms), and parliamentary rights, combined with Charles I's specific mismanagement and personal rigidity.
